subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Planning Fallacy: Why Everything Takes Longer
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Planning Fallacy: Why Everything Takes Longer.

hook.text: The Sydney Opera House: estimated 4 years and $7M. Actual: 16 years and $102M. This happens to every project everywhere.

buildup.text: The planning fallacy: we consistently underestimate time, cost, and risk for projects while overestimating benefits.

discovery.text: Kahneman: we plan from the 'inside view' – our specific project.

twist.text: Knowing about the planning fallacy doesn't fix it.

climax.text: The fix: 'reference class forecasting.' Find 10 similar projects. Use their average completion time, not yours.

punchline.text: Your estimate is wrong. Use history's estimate instead.

quiz.question: What is 'reference class forecasting'?
options: Using completion data from similar past projects to predict your own
Planning based on the best case scenario

details.summary: The planning fallacy is the systematic tendency to underestimate the time, cost, and risk of future actions while overestimating their benefits. It persists even when you have repeatedly experienced delays in similar past projects.
details.whyItMatters: The planning fallacy explains chronic lateness in construction, software, and personal projects. It wastes resources and erodes trust.
takeaways: People consistently underestimate time and cost for future tasks
Past experience with delays does not cure the bias
Reference class forecasting is the best known corrective

faq.question: Why does experience with past delays not fix the planning fallacy?
faq.answer: People treat each new project as unique, believing this time will be different. They focus on the ideal scenario rather than base rates of similar projects. The inside view consistently overrides lessons from the outside view.

faq.question: What is reference class forecasting and how does it help?
faq.answer: Instead of planning from the inside, look at how long similar projects actually took. If comparable kitchen renovations average 8 months, your plan of 4 months is likely optimistic regardless of your specific circumstances.
